name: IL-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with +18 partisan lean
Donna Miller's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Republican nominee has raised essentially nothing
model.rationale: The +18 Democratic lean and open-seat fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and Miller's $2.4 million raised plus $4.5 million in outside support dwarfs a Republican campaign with no reported fundraising. Markets price this near-certain for Democrats, so the forecast stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually low-turnout special dynamic could narrow the margin, though not the likely winner.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Robin Kelly (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Robin Kelly's retirement leaves this heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat open, but the district's +18 Democratic lean makes a party flip very unlikely. Democrat Donna Miller enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million raised and more than $4.5 million in outside support backing her, while Republican Michael Noack shows no reported fundraising or outside spending.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects a Democratic hold by a wide, though somewhat reduced, margin given the open seat and the absence of public polling.
